author: TEDx Talks
description:
Money doesn’t break families. Silence does. 

In this TEDx talk, Anneleen challenges families, entrepreneurs and leaders to engage in the conversations about wealth they’ve been avoiding, and shows why avoidance, not disagreement, is the real risk.

Anneleen Michiels is a professor of finance who studies what happens when money and human relationships collide across generations. For over fifteen years, she has examined how wealth and ownership influence decision-making, conflict, and legacy in families and organizations worldwide. As the author of Money & Generations, Anneleen translates rigorous academic insight into ideas that change how people think and talk about money, responsibility, and the future. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: How to talk to your family about money | Anneleen Michiels | TEDxUHasselt

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the reason you can't find your niche isn't a lack of clarity, but a lifetime of experience that doesn't fit neatly into one label? 

In this personal, humorous and emotional TEDx talk, business and mindset coach Rani Peluso shares how a devastating encounter with a mentor led her to question everything she knew about herself and how her unlikely background in computer programming helped her rediscover her confidence. 

Her story challenges conventional career and business advice, revealing why recognising the patterns in your own life may be more powerful than allowing someone else to decide who you should become. Rani Peluso is a business and mindset coach, author and founder of RANI COACHING, with more than 23 years of experience in coaching and personal development. She holds a BSc (Hons) in Science and Computing from London, UK, and spent 15 years working in investment banking before building her coaching business. 

An Advanced Demartini Method Facilitator, Rani has devel
title: Why ‘Just Pick a Niche’ Is Bad Advice | Rani Peluso | TEDxAlmansorParkStudio

Her talk explores the relationship between change, innovation, and human responsibility, reminding us that the future is not simply something we wait for but something we help create. A Middle School and High School teacher at Sinarmas World Academy. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description:
Thirty years ago, Jackie Chambers de Freitas walked into her first server room and counted. She was the only Black woman there. That experience gave her a perspective she would spend decades learning to understand. Drawing on her career in technology leadership, Jackie challenges a common assumption: the people a system fails first aren't exceptions to dismiss. They may be the most accurate source of information about what isn't working. She reveals why the view from the edge can help us build better systems for everyone. Jackie Chambers de Freitas is VP of AI Delivery & Transformation at Salesforce, where she leads initiatives that turn artificial intelligence into measurable business value. With more than 30 years of experience, she has helped global organizations accelerate innovation, improve efficiency, and drive business results. She spoke at RenderATL 2026 on moving AI beyond prototypes into real-world impact.

A British woman with Jamaican roots and an HBCU alumna, Jackie is p
title: The People Your System Fails First | Jackie Chambers de Freitas | TEDxBuckheadAve

author: TEDx Talks
description: Aadi considers the language organisations reach for when they have something difficult to say, and what is lost when a decision is described in terms that make it sound inevitable. Drawing on examples from business, medicine, and sport, he looks at the difference between wording chosen to protect the listener and wording chosen to protect the speaker. Aadi is a Year 11 pupil at King's College School, Wimbledon, with a particular passion for science and linguistics. He is fascinated by how scientific discovery helps us understand the world, and by how words across different languages shape the way we communicate with, interact with, and respect others. Beyond the classroom, he plays cricket and racquet sports, and nurtures his love of music through the piano and violin. He also follows Formula 1 and enjoys designing and racing model cars. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.c
title: What our words reveal that our actions cannot | Aadi Jhawar | TEDxKings College School

description: Arjun looks at a series of discoveries in science and in food that began with something going wrong, from penicillin to polyethylene. His interest is in what the people involved did next, and in why an accident becomes a discovery for some and a wasted afternoon for others. Arjun is a Year 8 pupil at King's College School, Wimbledon, who loves Mathematics and Science and is passionate about learning new things. Outside the classroom, he runs a school club with some of his friends. In his free time, he plays squash and cricket, and enjoys reading and the occasional video game. He is also an avid chess player and represents both the school and Surrey at chess. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: Direct Air Capture proposes to remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere after it has been released. Anthony assesses how realistic this is, working through the energy costs the chemistry imposes and the question of who would pay for the technology at scale. His conclusion is measured rather than either dismissive or optimistic. Anthony is a sixth form pupil at King's College School, Wimbledon. He is studying the International Baccalaureate, taking Mathematics, Physics, and Chemistry at higher level. He hopes to study Engineering at university and was recently awarded an Arkwright Engineering Scholarship, sponsored by the Royal Air Force. He is also a keen sportsman, with a passion for rugby and rock climbing, and enjoys volunteering with his local Scout group. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

description: Nicholas's great-grandfather served with the Chindits in Burma, a force that rarely appears in accounts of the Second World War. Beginning with his own family research, and taking in a nineteenth-century Ethiopian emperor and the world's oldest writing system, he makes a case for the parts of history that sit behind the famous names and dates. Nicholas is a Year 10 pupil at King's College School, Wimbledon. He enjoys all his academic subjects, but is particularly passionate about History and Classics. Alongside his academic studies, he is a keen musician. He is a member of the English Schools Orchestra and principal horn in the Stoneleigh Youth Orchestra. At school, he enjoys debating, hockey, tennis, and reading club. In his free time, he likes Lego and reading books about history. author: TEDx Talks
description: Leo examines the gap between what we say we want and what we actually do, a problem philosophers have worried about for a very long time and which most of us encounter before breakfast. He then asks what it means for institutions, from voting to sentencing, that are designed around the assumption that people know their own minds. Leo is a Year 11 pupil at King's College School, Wimbledon, who is passionate about philosophy, politics, and the delicate link between the two. He has a particular interest in theology, and is a founding member of "Big Questions and the Bible", a club which explores profound questions through a religious lens. Outside school, he enjoys rugby, football, and cricket, and is a keen supporter of AFC Wimbledon. He also loves music and travelling. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Can humanity ever know what it really wants? | Leo McCann | TEDxKings College School

What happens when you grow up in one language and suddenly have to live in another? After moving from Shanghai to Singapore at 14, I found myself becoming somehow different—not just in how I spoke, but in who I was. In this talk, I reflect on my feelings about living between different languages, places, and identities, exploring multiple versions of ourselves, and how that might be what makes us whole. Jiaqi (Emily) is a 17-year-old student currently studying at Chatsworth. She grew up in Shanghai, China, and spent the first 14 years of her life there. She came to Singapore by herself when she was 15, and it made her start thinking about some questions she had never thought about before—identity, language, and what it means to feel whole.

Growing up, she always had a burning passion for telling stories of all kinds, whether it be fiction or not, and her passion of telling stories is her motivational drive. Her passion is what drives her, and what drives her can spark endless possibilities and opportunities. Khione is a student at an International School in Singapore. She believes this is the age to explore, so she has tried to say yes to as many things as possible. description:
In this talk, Petrina Kow unpacks some of the physiology around breathing and voice. Breath occupies the most active place in human vocal production: it is the energy impulse that excites the vibration in the vocal folds and the resulting resonance in the body. Petrina highlights how the way in which the human body breathes impacts the voice a great deal, much as the hands of a good pianist and a beginner create different sounds with the same instrument.
 Petrina Kow  is a voice, accents, and public speaking coach with over 25 years of experience working with C-suite executives, award-winning actors, and professional speakers. She helps individuals and teams communicate with clarity, confidence, and authenticity through private coaching and group workshops. Her clients include global organizations such as Google, Roche Diagnostics, HSBC, Nickelodeon, Disney, and Netflix. title: On Speaking as a Whole | Petrina Kow | TEDxChatsworthInternationalSchool

description: What does it mean to build a legacy when you are reminded that time is not guaranteed? Michael Bays shares a deeply personal story about cancer, fatherhood, resilience, and the meaning we create through the lives we live. Rather than focusing only on the challenges he has faced, his talk explores what those experiences have taught him about being present, choosing what matters, and showing up for the people we love. His story asks us to reconsider the idea of legacy, not as something we leave behind someday, but as something we are creating through our choices every day. 1997 Clemson Graduate in Business Management and 1999 Masters Degree in Human Resources Development. While at Clemson, Michael was the Tiger Mascot and held the Career Push Up Record. He currently works as an Executive Recruiter and is also a 3 Time 20 year Cancer Survivor. author: TEDx Talks
description: What does it take to send humanity back to the Moon? Charlie Blackwell-Thompson, NASA's first Artemis launch director, takes audiences behind one of the most ambitious endeavors in modern space exploration. She shares her personal journey to leading the launch of Artemis and explores the larger vision behind the program. Artemis represents a series of increasingly complex missions designed to establish a lasting human presence on the Moon and create new possibilities for exploration beyond it. Her story offers a firsthand look at the people, preparation, and purpose behind humanity's next steps into the cosmos. Charlie Blackwell-Thompson is NASA’s Artemis Launch Director and the first woman to serve as a launch director for NASA’s Exploration Ground Systems Program. A Clemson University graduate originally from Gaffney, South Carolina, she has spent more than three decades contributing to human spaceflight, from Space Shuttle operations to the Artemis missions. title: Going First, Inspiring Others To Go Further | Charlie Blackwell-Thompson | TEDxClemson U

description: In this inspiring TEDx talk, Avani Awasthi shares how her dream of saving the planet evolved from pursuing dramatic change to embracing small, consistent actions. Drawing from her experiences in Antarctica, motherhood, and sustainable entrepreneurship, she introduces her "1% Challenge" and shows how tiny daily habits can create lasting impact for people and the planet Avani Awasthee is an environmental crusader, sustainability entrepreneur, and one of the youngest Indians to travel to Antarctica as an Environmental Ambassador. From advocating for climate action on global platforms to building a sustainable fashion brand rooted in conscious living, she has dedicated her work to creating a better future for generations to come. Today, she shares how individual choices, driven by purpose, can create extraordinary impact. description: How much do we really know about the Native communities that have shaped South Carolina? Joshua Shumak challenges common assumptions and misconceptions surrounding Native American history and identity. As a leader within the Wassamasaw Tribe of Varnertown Indians, he brings a personal perspective to conversations about tribal communities, cultural identity, and the Native presence that continues today. His talk invites audiences to look beyond historical stereotypes and develop a deeper understanding of the people, traditions, and communities that remain an important part of South Carolina. Joshua Shumak is a public servant and cultural practitioner who has worked in public tribal affairs for over a decade, supporting Native communities through statewide engagement, program development, and advocacy. Through powerful personal stories, he challenges the belief that life always demands an “either-or” choice and introduces the transformative mindset of “AND” as a way to pursue dreams, responsibilities, education, and success together. His story is a testament to resilience, possibility, and the power of refusing to choose limits Bala Nadar is the Founder of Startupwala, a platform that has helped thousands of entrepreneurs transform ideas into businesses. Passionate about democratizing entrepreneurship, he has spent years enabling aspiring founders to navigate the challenges of starting and growing ventures. description: In this thought-provoking TEDx talk, Kaivalya Deo explores how curiosity, questions, and books have shaped his understanding of the world. Drawing insights from literature, history, human evolution, and personal experiences, he reveals how reading empowers us to challenge assumptions, think critically, and create meaningful change. Kaivalya's message is simple yet powerful: we may run out of answers, but we should never run out of questions Kaivalya is a passionate reader and accomplished student whose love for literature earned him the Avid Reader Trophy for three consecutive years. An enthusiastic explorer of mythology, history, and fiction, he is also an award-winning performer in poem recitation, storytelling, and drama. Having represented his school at various inter-school events, Kaivalya exemplifies curiosity, creativity, and the power of reading to inspire young minds. Mathematics is often thought of as a collection of formulas and answers, but at its heart, it’s a process of discovery. Neil Calkin and Eliza Gallagher invite us to look at mathematics through a different lens—one centered on curiosity, exploration, patterns, and unexpected connections. Their talk demonstrates how mathematical thinking can emerge from seemingly simple questions and how the process of figuring something out can be just as meaningful as arriving at the answer. description: In a world where technology can increasingly provide answers, what happens to our ability to ask better questions? Meegan Kriley-Mackay explores the power of curiosity in an increasingly AI-driven world. Her talk examines how curiosity can help us navigate uncertainty, understand complex problems, and connect more meaningfully with others. Rather than allowing technology to replace our sense of wonder, she challenges us to use it as an opportunity to become even more curious about the world around us. Meegan Kriley-Mackay is a Human Intelligence (HI) Subject Matter Expert, Speaker, and former U.S. Department of Defense interrogator who studies how command, control, and coercion shut down HI, while curiosity reboots it. Through her work in leadership development and crisis response training with law enforcement and emergency responders, she applies real-world insights to help people think more clearly and respond effectively under stress. title: How Interrogation Helped Me Discover Myself | Meegan Kriley-Mackay | TEDxClemson U

Every single tatkaar, chakkar, mudra, and expression allows the dancer to understand that the most extraordinary moments come unexpectedly. Sleep deprivation has become a modern epidemic, affecting nearly all of our lives. But how bad is it really? This talk explores what happens when we consistently sacrifice sleep, from impaired focus, memory, and reaction time to nightmares and sleep paralysis, and challenges us to rethink the late nights we’ve come to see as normal. author: TEDx Talks
description:
We are entering a post-literate society where attention has become a commodity, scrolling is replacing deep reading, and even education risks becoming a form of infotainment. At the same time, artificial intelligence is making it increasingly easy to outsource not only information gathering, but also reasoning and decision-making.
What, then, distinguishes human thought from machine intelligence? This talk explores self-awareness, emotion, lived experience, and our ability to create meaning and make independent choices. It also reconsiders the role of universities as places where people can think freely, debate, and pursue knowledge beyond efficiency or productivity.
As AI becomes more deeply embedded in our lives, this talk asks how we can preserve human agency and our capacity to think for ourselves. Ultimately, it invites us to reconsider a fundamental question: what does it mean to remain human in the age of AI?

Have you ever felt pressured or feared failure in your daily life because you were so focused on pursuing your ultimate goals or results? As a result, you may have overlooked the process of getting there and missed the small discoveries right in front of you. 
What is Troy Yoshimoto’s approach to daily life? He works as an industrial designer in New York, designing products we use in our daily lives, while also pursuing a career in ceramics in Kyoto. Drawing inspiration for his work from nature, respecting and loving it, he shares what he believes is essential for living a life filled with joy and curiosity.

Unele visuri se nasc în copilărie și ne însoțesc o viață întreagă.
Povestea lui Marlene și Dinu Mititeanu vorbește despre pasiunea pentru munte, despre două drumuri unite de același vis și despre perseverența de a merge mai departe, indiferent de vârstă sau de dificultățile întâlnite.
Pentru că visurile, singure, nu ne duc până pe vârf. Dar, pas cu pas, cu răbdare și perseverență, ele se pot transforma într-un mod de viață.
 Dinu Mititeanu is an iconic figure in Romanian mountaineering and mountain education, often described as the "conscience of the mountains." He embodies ageless youth: even in his eighties, he continues to hike and climb mountain trails. Marlene Mititeanu is much more than "the wife who accompanies him"—she is a symbol of unwavering loyalty. In a world shaped by individualism, Marlene represents the idea that the highest peaks are climbed together. author: TEDx Talks
description: Why are teenagers considered too young to make important decisions, while at the same time living through the most adaptable period of their lives? In this thought-provoking talk, Yasemin Erol challenges the way society views adolescence by exploring the science of neuroplasticity and the remarkable ability of the teenage brain to reshape itself. Through examples from everyday habits, social media, and personal growth, she argues that the choices we repeat today become the foundation of who we are tomorrow. Rather than asking young people what they want to be, she invites them to ask a more important question: Who do I want to become? Because our future is not simply something we grow into—it is something we actively write, one thought, habit, and decision at a time. Yasemin Erol is a 10th-grade student at Üsküdar American Academy in Istanbul.
